decision: How A2 Acquire Dated Evidence (C.2) asks its sources
status_of_judgments: The importance levels and the hours below are proposals awaiting the team's confirmation (2026-11-21). The raw figures of EC.1 to EC.4 are measured or read from the product.

alternatives.name: Parallel acquisition with half the market request spacing
alternatives.model: SC.2 with the shorter spacing (no scenario of its own)

importance_levels.critical: the product fails its purpose without it
importance_levels.important: the product is clearly worse without it

variation_levels.large: the alternatives differ by a large part of the acceptable range
variation_levels.medium: they differ, and no alternative leaves the acceptable range
variation_levels.small: they are equal or nearly equal

criteria.name: Time to the answer
criteria.metric: mean time from RUN pressed to the report ready, live sources
criteria.source: Measured: 10 live runs of each alternative on 2026-11-21 (data/timings/ch11_*, scripts/measure_runs.py). Worst level = the limit of NFR.1; best level = an assumption (a wait a first-time reader accepts without a progress page).

criteria.name: Standing with the market data source
criteria.metric: peak request rate to the source that publishes no limit
criteria.source: Read from the product: one request each 0.5 s (settings.market_min_interval_seconds) is 2 a second; 0.25 s is 4 a second. Best level = the rate the product has run at since October with no throttled response in 50 measured runs. Worst level = an assumption: Yahoo publishes no rate, and its terms restrict automated access (legal.yahoo.com terms, section 2(d), read 2026-11-21); 10 a second is the SEC's stated maximum, taken as the outer bound.

criteria.name: Completion when a source is down
criteria.metric: share of the other source's steps that still end ok when one source refuses every request
criteria.source: Measured by test: tests/test_acquisition_mode.py::test_a_source_that_is_down_costs_only_its_own_steps, both modes, each source down in turn. AL.3 runs the code of AL.2.

criteria.name: Same record on replay
criteria.metric: share of a replayed case's fields equal to the sequential record, clock times apart

criteria.name: Life cycle cost
criteria.metric: team hours to build and keep for two years
criteria.source: Assumption (hours, see life_cycle_cost). No alternative adds a paid source or a paid request (CR.2.0.2).

assumptions: Hours are extra hours over the sequential product; the upkeep both share is left out.
Build: writing, reviewing and testing the two lanes (124 lines added, 25 removed in three files, and 11 tests).
Upkeep of AL.2: keeping the lane code and its tests working as steps are added.
Upkeep of AL.3: the same, and watching for throttled responses and retuning the spacing when the source changes its behaviour.
Rate: 50 USD an hour, a stand-in for a graduate engineer's time. Budget: 40 hours, what the team can still give this term.
